claims.text: The as-synthesized (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy exhibits a large caloric response under applied magnetic fields.
The as-synthesized alloy exhibits a large caloric response under applied pressure fields.
The as-synthesized alloy has poor mechanical integrity and is prone to cracking.
Adding approximately 1–2 wt% Si and C is an appropriate intervention for this alloy.
Si and C additions can react in situ to form SiC particles in a high-entropy-alloy matrix.
The proposed processing will produce nanoscale SiC precipitates in (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38.
The SiC precipitates will be distributed both along grain boundaries and within grains.
Controlled cooling or heat treatment can produce a fine, uniform SiC dispersion in this alloy.
SiC particles will impede crack initiation and propagation.
SiC particles will pin grain boundaries.
SiC reinforcement will provide dispersion-related strengthening.
SiC reinforcement will increase the alloy's load-bearing capacity.
The modified alloy will have greater hardness than the unchanged alloy.
The modified alloy will have greater fracture toughness than the unchanged alloy.
The modified alloy will exhibit less cracking than the unchanged alloy.
SiC precipitation will leave the primary caloric phase transition largely unaltered.
The modified alloy will retain entropy and temperature changes comparable to the unchanged alloy under magnetic-field operation.
The modified alloy will retain entropy and temperature changes comparable to the unchanged alloy under pressure-field operation.
The intervention will function near room temperature or at the caloric transition temperature under the same magnetic and pressure fields used for refrigeration.

contradictions.description: The falsification rule defines failure as no statistically significant integrity improvement, but its parenthetical description includes 'reduced cracking,' which is itself a predicted improvement rather than evidence of failure.
